additions.name: AI + Wearable Sensors

justifications.healthTech.industryPlacement: Direct exposure to FDA-cleared sensor platforms creates concrete entry points into digital health and remote monitoring vendors.
justifications.healthTech.vendorDemand: Wearable and remote monitoring vendors actively recruit clinicians who can validate algorithms and design clinical workflows.
justifications.healthTech.salaryPremium: Moderate premium for clinical SMEs in wearable/RPM startups, though not at the level of dedicated ML/engineering hires.
justifications.healthTech.technicalSkillDepth: Hands-on familiarity with sensor accuracy, signal interpretation, and AI-derived metrics builds genuine technical fluency.
justifications.healthTech.transitionFit: One of the cleanest bridges from clinical work into medtech/digital health roles such as clinical specialist or product clinician.
justifications.healthTech.efficiency: Short certification footprint relative to the career optionality it opens.
justifications.research.methodologyDepth: Exposure to sensor validation studies introduces measurement science but not full research methods training.
justifications.research.publicationTrack: Sensor validation and digital biomarker work is a publishable niche with growing journal interest.
justifications.research.grantReadiness: Aligns with NIH digital health and NSF smart health funding lines as a clinical co-investigator role.
justifications.research.pathwayToIndependence: Useful as a domain area but does not on its own train someone to lead independent research.
justifications.research.interdisciplinaryFit: Natural meeting point for clinicians, data scientists, and engineers.
justifications.research.efficiency: Modest time/cost relative to research-relevant skill gained.

additions.rationale: Wearables + AI is a core HealthTech competency and one of the few clinical certs that meaningfully signals technical depth; it also bridges into clinical-validation research roles.

additions.name: VR (Medical-Grade)

justifications.healthTech.industryPlacement: FDA-cleared VR rehab vendors (MindMaze, XRHealth, AppliedVR) hire clinical specialists for deployment and content development.
justifications.healthTech.vendorDemand: Growing but still niche demand from a small set of VR therapeutics companies.
justifications.healthTech.salaryPremium: Modest premium; most roles are clinical-specialist tier rather than engineering.
justifications.healthTech.technicalSkillDepth: Builds familiarity with XR platforms, content design, and outcome measurement but limited true engineering depth.
justifications.healthTech.transitionFit: Reasonable bridge for clinicians wanting to enter digital therapeutics.
justifications.healthTech.efficiency: Vendor-specific training is relatively short for the door it opens.

additions.rationale: Medical-grade VR is one of the few rehab-side credentials with a clear vendor ecosystem and digital-therapeutics career path.

additions.name: Virtual/Augmented Reality

justifications.healthTech.industryPlacement: Vendor-specific XR training feeds into a small but expanding set of digital therapeutic companies.
justifications.healthTech.vendorDemand: Demand exists but is fragmented across vendors and still maturing.
justifications.healthTech.salaryPremium: Limited premium given thin evidence base and immature reimbursement.
justifications.healthTech.technicalSkillDepth: Exposure to XR development concepts without core engineering skill.
justifications.healthTech.transitionFit: Provides a credible entry signal for clinicians moving into XR product/clinical roles.
justifications.healthTech.efficiency: Short vendor courses relative to optionality created.

additions.rationale: Broader VR/AR training is a weaker but legitimate HealthTech signal; scored lower than medical-grade VR because of less clinical validation.

additions.name: Telehealth/Digital Health

justifications.healthTech.industryPlacement: Telehealth and digital health platforms (Hinge, SWORD, Omada, Kaia) actively hire clinicians with digital delivery experience.
justifications.healthTech.vendorDemand: Strong and sustained demand from virtual-first MSK and chronic-disease companies.
justifications.healthTech.salaryPremium: Moderate premium for clinical leadership in digital-first care.
justifications.healthTech.technicalSkillDepth: Skills are more workflow/platform than engineering; depth is moderate at best.
justifications.healthTech.transitionFit: One of the most direct on-ramps from clinic to digital health employer.
justifications.healthTech.efficiency: Skills-based training is low-cost relative to career mobility gained.

additions.rationale: Digital health platforms are the largest single HealthTech employer of clinicians; telehealth training is a credible (if not engineering-grade) signal.

additions.name: Telehealth Cardiac/Pulmonary

justifications.healthTech.industryPlacement: Remote cardiac/pulmonary monitoring vendors (BioIntelliSense, Cleerly, Recora) hire clinicians for program design.
justifications.healthTech.vendorDemand: Steady demand driven by Medicare RPM/RTM reimbursement expansion.
justifications.healthTech.salaryPremium: Modest premium for niche clinical expertise on RPM teams.
justifications.healthTech.technicalSkillDepth: Combines clinical protocol design with wearable/RPM integration knowledge.
justifications.healthTech.transitionFit: Clear pathway into virtual cardiac/pulmonary rehab companies.
justifications.healthTech.efficiency: Moderate-cost training with reasonable career payoff.

additions.rationale: Specialty telehealth in cardiac/pulm is a real and reimbursed HealthTech segment with a defined vendor landscape.

additions.name: Exoskeleton Training

justifications.healthTech.industryPlacement: Ekso, ReWalk, Indego, and Wandercraft hire clinical specialists and trainers.
justifications.healthTech.vendorDemand: Small vendor pool but each has dedicated clinical-specialist roles.
justifications.healthTech.salaryPremium: Moderate premium for device-specialist roles at robotics vendors.
justifications.healthTech.technicalSkillDepth: Builds genuine familiarity with robotic gait device mechanics and patient programming.
justifications.healthTech.transitionFit: Direct bridge into medical-robotics industry roles.
justifications.healthTech.efficiency: High training investment relative to small vendor market.

additions.rationale: Exoskeleton certification is one of the most concrete medtech-vendor credentials in rehab, with named industry employers.

additions.name: Robotic Devices (Lokomat)

justifications.healthTech.industryPlacement: Hocoma and similar robotics vendors employ clinical specialists for deployment and training.
justifications.healthTech.vendorDemand: Narrow but consistent vendor demand for trained clinicians.
justifications.healthTech.salaryPremium: Modest premium for robotics vendor clinical roles.
justifications.healthTech.technicalSkillDepth: Hands-on with complex robotic gait systems builds technical literacy.

additions.rationale: Lokomat-class device training is vendor-specific and a recognized credential among rehab-robotics manufacturers.

additions.name: Robotic Upper Limb

justifications.healthTech.industryPlacement: Bionik (InMotion), Tyromotion, and Kinarm hire clinical specialists.
justifications.healthTech.vendorDemand: Small vendor ecosystem with steady clinical-specialist demand.
justifications.healthTech.salaryPremium: Modest premium aligned with rehab robotics roles.
justifications.healthTech.technicalSkillDepth: Direct work with sensor-instrumented robotic devices builds device literacy.
justifications.healthTech.transitionFit: Defined pathway into upper-limb robotics vendor roles.

additions.rationale: Like Lokomat, upper-limb robotics is a small but real medtech segment with named employers.

additions.name: Assistive Technology Professional (ATP)

justifications.healthTech.industryPlacement: RESNA ATP is the standard credential for AT vendors (Permobil, Sunrise, Tobii Dynavox) hiring clinical reps.
justifications.healthTech.vendorDemand: Consistent demand from complex rehab and AAC manufacturers.
justifications.healthTech.salaryPremium: Modest premium; ATP is often a requirement for industry roles rather than a bonus.
justifications.healthTech.technicalSkillDepth: Develops practical fluency across mobility, AAC, EADL, and sensor-based AT.
justifications.healthTech.transitionFit: One of the most established clinical-to-industry credentials in AT/medtech.
justifications.healthTech.efficiency: Reasonable cost relative to industry recognition.

additions.rationale: ATP is explicitly the industry-standard credential for assistive-technology manufacturers and a true HealthTech bridge.

additions.name: Seating and Mobility Specialist

justifications.healthTech.industryPlacement: Complex rehab technology vendors (Permobil, Quantum, Ki Mobility) recruit SMS-credentialed clinicians.
justifications.healthTech.vendorDemand: Steady demand within complex rehab manufacturers and dealers.
justifications.healthTech.salaryPremium: Modest premium for vendor clinical-education roles.
justifications.healthTech.technicalSkillDepth: Builds engineering-adjacent knowledge of seating systems, power components, and electronics.
justifications.healthTech.transitionFit: Recognized pathway into complex rehab industry.
justifications.healthTech.efficiency: Moderate training burden with defined industry pay-off.

additions.rationale: SMS, like ATP, is a credential explicitly recognized by complex-rehab manufacturers and a legitimate HealthTech bridge.

additions.name: Transitional DPT (tDPT)

justifications.research.methodologyDepth: Most tDPT programs include EBP and research-methods coursework, but at a lighter level than a research doctorate.
justifications.research.publicationTrack: Some capstone work is publishable but the degree is not designed to produce a publication record.
justifications.research.grantReadiness: Limited grant training; insufficient on its own to lead funded research.
justifications.research.pathwayToIndependence: Acts as a credential bridge, not an independent-researcher pipeline; PhD/DSc is the real path.
justifications.research.interdisciplinaryFit: Coursework exposes clinicians to evidence synthesis across disciplines.
justifications.research.efficiency: Online, part-time format makes it relatively low-cost as a stepping stone.

additions.rationale: The tDPT is a credential-equivalency degree with modest research-methods exposure; it is a weak but real on-ramp toward a research doctorate, scored well below dedicated research credentials.

additions.name: ABCDEF ICU Bundle

justifications.research.methodologyDepth: Bundle training is grounded in implementation science methods and audit-and-feedback methodology.
justifications.research.publicationTrack: Implementation outcomes in ICU bundles are an active, publishable research line.
justifications.research.grantReadiness: Aligns with AHRQ and NHLBI implementation-science funding priorities.
justifications.research.pathwayToIndependence: Useful domain but not a standalone path to PI status.
justifications.research.interdisciplinaryFit: Inherently multi-professional (PT/OT/RT/RN/MD) and well-suited to team science.
justifications.research.efficiency: Low training cost relative to research-domain entry it provides.

additions.rationale: ABCDEF is one of the few clinical protocols with a substantive implementation-science research footprint, making it a legitimate but secondary research bridge.
